blocks.heading: The purpose of business activity
blocks.text: Business activity organises resources to provide goods or services that satisfy wants and needs. A need is something essential for living, while a want is a particular way someone would like a need or desire satisfied. Producing something is not sufficient for commercial success: the offer must reach customers at a price and quality they accept. A private enterprise normally seeks enough revenue to cover costs and provide a return; other organisations may prioritise a service or social objective.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Omuti Foods is an invented small bakery supplying bread to families in a Namibian town. The bakery combines ingredients, equipment and people to make bread available locally. Customers obtain food without baking it themselves, while sales give the bakery revenue with which to pay its costs. Revenue is not the same as profit: costs must be deducted. A shortage of customers or rising costs can prevent an otherwise useful business from surviving.
